title: Adapted Fröhlich-Pizzo Model for Horizon-Induced Decoherence
abstract: The Fröhlich-Pizzo (FP) model is a quantum-mechanical model originally developed to describe the interaction between an atom and the electromagnetic field in the nonrelativistic limit $c\to\infty$. We show that an adaptation of the FP model based on the local algebras of a $U(1)$ chiral current captures essential features of the horizon-induced decoherence mechanism identified by Danielson, Satishchandran, and Wald (DSW) in the limit of large holding time $T$. Our analysis suggests that the effective dynamics of the system undergoing decoherence in the DSW setting retains non-Markovian features. Our approach also offers a glimpse into the possible role of quantum events in the dynamics underlying horizon-induced decoherence.
summary: This theoretical paper adapts the Fröhlich-Pizzo model to study decoherence induced by a black hole horizon. By applying the Events-Trees-Histories framework, the authors show that while the asymptotic decoherence matches prior work, residual correlations suggest the underlying dynamics are non-Markovian. This implies the horizon geometry may fundamentally influence the algebraic structure of quantum events.
main_problem: The paper investigates the connection between the Events–Trees–Histories (ETH) approach to quantum mechanics and the phenomenon of horizon-induced decoherence near a Killing horizon.
main_result: The adapted Fröhlich-Pizzo model successfully reproduces the asymptotic decoherence predicted by DSW, but reveals residual vacuum correlations suggesting the underlying dynamics may retain non-Markovian features.
method: The authors adapt the Fröhlich-Pizzo model using local algebras of a U(1) chiral current to analyze the reduced state of a charged particle interacting with the horizon degrees of freedom.
model_or_system: The system involves a charged particle near a Killing horizon, modeled using an adaptation of the Fröhlich-Pizzo (FP) model. This framework is analyzed through the lens of the ETH approach, focusing on the structure of quantum events.
key_observables: Off-diagonal Gram coefficients, residual vacuum correlations, and the structure of the centralizer of the combined system.
important_parameters: Large holding time (T), the logarithm of the affine null coordinate along the horizon.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on adapting the FP model to handle the continuum nature of the horizon degrees of freedom, contrasting with the original discrete FP model.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by reviewing the ETH approach, the FP model, and the DSW decoherence mechanism before proposing and analyzing the adapted FP model to address the continuum horizon structure.
why_interesting: The work bridges quantum foundations (ETH) with quantum gravity effects (horizon decoherence), suggesting that fundamental algebraic structures (like those governing quantum events) might be influenced by spacetime geometry.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic illustration of the horizon cuts and their associated wedge regions. (a) The bifurcation surface is denoted by B, and the green dot represents the codimension-two cross-section V = λ of the future horizon. The portion of the horizon to the future of this cut is denoted by Σ+ λ (red). The red and blue lines bound the right wedge Wλ and its causal complement W ′ λ, respectively. (b) Two horizon cuts with λ′ > λ. The corresponding wedge regions are nested, Wλ′ ⊂Wλ, as are the future portions of the horizon, Σ+ λ′ ⊂Σ+ λ .
